hero.lede: I am collaborating with numerous like-minded peers to investigate the upper bound of intelligence. Concurrently, I have a strong research interest in foundational data construction and model evaluation, which I regard as the basis for intelligence development and the cornerstone underlying its upper bound.

about.heading: Personal Resume
paragraphs: I am an incoming M.S. student in the School of Cyber Science and Engineering at Southeast University. I received my undergraduate training at the School of Artificial Intelligence, South China Normal University, under the supervision of Prof. Jiahui Pan. My research interests include multimodal reasoning, affective computing, foundational data construction, and model evaluation. I aim to conduct further meaningful research and welcome collaborations with interested researchers.

glance.value: Multimodal Reasoning · Affective Computing · Foundational Data Construction, and Model Evaluation

research.heading: What I work on
research.sub: My research focuses on four areas: Multimodal Reasoning · Affective Computing · Foundational Data Construction, and Model Evaluation. I am dedicated to probing the upper bound of intelligence through multimodal reasoning. Although it is often regarded as a plug-in, I intend to drive iterative model refinement through large-scale data and model evaluation. Furthermore, motivated by personal interest, I will investigate downstream applications of multimodal large models / large models in affective computing.

items.title: Multimodal Reasoning
items.text: Joint inference over language, vision, and other modalities. Rather than a single fused classifier, I am interested in general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that can reason about why a state holds and answer follow-up questions about it.

items.title: Affective Computing
items.text: Estimating emotional and cognitive states from physiological signals as part of a general-purpose world model. The goal is a model whose state estimates are stable enough to trust outside the lab.
Two papers accepted to **IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing**
Paper on multi-dimensional feature fusion and multi-level domain adaptation accepted to **ICASSP 2026**.
*PR-DA* accepted to **IEEE BIBM 2025**; code released on GitHub.
Paper on progressive multi-domain adaptation published in **IEEE TNSRE** — with code.
